links.outcome: LLM accommodation of harmful beliefs varying with linguistic encoding of the same premise
links.effect: Social and linguistic factors (at-issueness, linguistic encoding, source reliability) affect LLM accommodation and explain performance differences across three safety benchmarks (Cancer-Myth, SAGE-Eval, ELEPHANT).
links.quote: We show that social and linguistic factors known to influence accommodation in humans (at-issueness, linguistic encoding, and source reliability) similarly affect accommodation in LLMs, explaining performance differences across three safety benchmarks that test models' ability to challenge harmful beliefs, spanning misinformation (Cancer-Myth, SAGE-Eval) and sycophancy (ELEPHANT).

unlisted_practices: Adding pragmatic prompt interventions (e.g., 'wait a minute') to make LLMs challenge users' harmful beliefs while keeping false-positive rates low

screen.reason: The study empirically tests LLM performance on safety benchmarks including health/medical misinformation (Cancer-Myth) and evaluates a simple prompt guardrail ('wait a minute') to reduce sycophancy and failure to challenge harmful beliefs.

primary.practice: pragmatic prompting guardrail to challenge harmful beliefs
